payload.claim: `describe()`'s `Baseline` branch is an if/else that returns early when `event.aborted` is non-empty, producing only the 'baseline errored in [...] — the toolchain is broken, not the code' line. But the real call site (`saffron/cell/session.py:871-882`) prints the joined 'baseline: g=s, ...' line *unconditionally* first, and only then, if aborted, prints the second 'baseline errored in ...' line as well — so on a toolchain-broken run the operator sees both lines today. Because `Baseline` bundles `aborted` together with `gates`/`statuses` on one dataclass, one `describe()` call can only ever reproduce one of the two, so whichever way `SA-0030` constructs this event (one event feeding one `watch(describe(event))` call, as the module's own docstring at line 439 promises), the per-gate status line is silently dropped exactly in the PREFLIGHT_FAILED case — the one where seeing which individual gates passed versus errored matters most for diagnosis.
